obama-foundation-leaders-africa-2027.about:
Obama Foundation Leaders Africa is a six-month virtual programme for people who are already driving change in their communities through the public, civil or private sector. The Foundation selects a cohort of emerging leaders from the region and connects them with peers, coaches and the wider Obama Leadership Network.

The curriculum is values-based: participants work on their own leadership, ethical decision-making and how to scale their impact, through virtual group sessions, peer-led learning spaces and individual coaching. After the programme, Leaders join a lifelong alumni network.

Applications for the 2027 cohort open on 9 November 2026 on the Foundation's site; the programme is free for selected participants.
highlights: Free, selective leadership programme from the Obama Foundation
Group sessions, peer learning and one-to-one coaching
Lifelong access to the Obama Leadership Network
obama-foundation-leaders-africa-2027.eligibility: Emerging leaders aged 24-45 during the programme, based in or connected to the Africa region, already working on change in the public, civil or private sector. Fluency in English is expected.
how_to_apply: Read the programme page and check the age and regional criteria.
Prepare a description of your work and its impact.
Submit the online application when it opens on 9 November 2026.
If shortlisted, complete the interview stage.
obama-foundation-leaders-africa-2027.costs: Free for selected participants. Any in-person convenings are organised by the Foundation; check the programme page for travel details.

oist-research-internship-fall-2027.about:
OIST is an English-language graduate university in Okinawa with an interdisciplinary research culture across physics, chemistry, biology, neuroscience, marine science, mathematics and computing. Its Research Internship lets students join a research unit of their choice for 4 to 6 months; the Fall 2027 round covers placements between 1 October 2027 and 31 March 2028.

Support is generous: one round-trip air ticket, furnished housing on or off campus, a stipend of JPY 2,400 per working day, visa help and a shuttle-bus pass. The internship is also a common route into OIST's fully funded PhD programme.
highlights: Choose any OIST research unit across the sciences
Flight, housing and JPY 2,400/working-day stipend covered
Common pathway to OIST's funded PhD
oist-research-internship-fall-2027.eligibility: Students in the last two years of a bachelor's degree or any year of a master's degree (in Japan or abroad), and bachelor's/master's graduates. Current or former PhD students are not eligible. Home-institution approval needed if enrolled.
how_to_apply: Browse OIST research units and pick the host you want
Prepare transcripts, a 250-word statement of purpose, CV, passport scan and ID photo
Ask 1–3 professors to submit recommendation letters (at least one must arrive before you submit)
Pay the JPY 5,000 application fee and submit by 15 April 2027 (23:59 JST)
Results are announced in mid-June 2027
oist-research-internship-fall-2027.costs: Free for interns: round-trip flight, furnished housing and a stipend of JPY 2,400 per working day. Application fee JPY 5,000 (non-refundable).

olimpiadi-informatica-2026-27.about:
The OII is promoted by the Italian Ministry of Education. Schools register on olimpiadi-scientifiche.it; students sit a school selection round, then territorial (regional) contests, and the best go to the national final, from which the IOI team is trained and chosen. A team championship (OIS) runs alongside.

Participation is free for both schools and students. All materials are in Italian.
highlights: Free for schools and students
School → regional → national rounds
Selects Italy's IOI team
olimpiadi-informatica-2026-27.eligibility: Upper-secondary students at Italian schools, registered by their school.
how_to_apply: Ask your school to register on olimpiadi-scientifiche.it
Train on the official training platform
Sit the school round, then regional and national rounds

open-door-international-school-exchange-.about:
Open Door International, a non-profit member of the AJA network since 1983, sends German school students aged 14/15-18 for a term, semester or school year (3, 4, 5 or 10 months) to Argentina, Costa Rica, Ecuador, France, Great Britain, Ireland, Canada, New Zealand, Spain and the USA, starting January/February or July-September.

Prices start at 6,490 euros (flights included for many programmes) with multi-day seminars before and after. Deadlines differ by country (see each country's programme details). ODI offers four partial scholarships worldwide per year; the 2027/28 ODI scholarship round closed on 30 October 2026, but partner scholarships remain.
highlights: 10 destination countries
From 6,490 euros
Non-profit AJA member
open-door-international-school-exchange-.eligibility: School students living in Germany aged about 15-18 (some countries 14).
how_to_apply: Pick a country and length on opendoorinternational.de
Check that country's deadline in the programme details
Apply online
Attend the pre-departure seminar
open-door-international-school-exchange-.costs: From 6,490 euros; partial ODI and partner scholarships.

optimist-international-essay-contest-202.about:
Optimist International's essay contest asks students to write an essay on the annual topic (length rules in the official contest materials). Entries are judged first at the local Optimist Club, then at district level, where winners compete for a $2,500 college scholarship funded by the Optimist International Foundations.

Optimist Clubs operate mainly in the United States, Canada and the Caribbean; deadlines are set by each club (club contests usually finish by late winter).
highlights: $2,500 district scholarships
Topic: 'Finding My Voice in a World Full of Noise'
Free, through local clubs
optimist-international-essay-contest-202.eligibility: Young people under 19 on 1 October 2026 who have not graduated high school, in areas served by an Optimist Club (US, Canada, Caribbean).
how_to_apply: Find your local Optimist Club via optimist.org
Ask the club for its entry deadline and forms
Write your essay on the 2026–27 topic
Submit to the club before its deadline

outreachy-may-2027.about:
Outreachy, a diversity initiative of Software Freedom Conservancy, offers paid, remote internships with open-source and open-science communities. Projects include programming, documentation, design, data science and community work, so you do not have to be an experienced programmer. The process has two stages: an initial application (essays about your background and the barriers you face), then a contribution period of about a month in which you make small contributions to projects before submitting a final application.

Interns work remotely for three months with experienced mentors and receive a USD 7,000 stipend. Outreachy is open to applicants around the world aged 18+ who face under-representation, systemic bias or discrimination in the tech industry of their country.
highlights: USD 7,000 stipend for a 3-month remote internship
No prior open-source experience needed
Open worldwide; focus on under-represented groups
outreachy-may-2027.eligibility: Applicants aged 18+ anywhere in the world who face under-representation, systemic bias or discrimination in tech in their country, and who are available full-time (about 30 hours/week) during the internship. Students must not have full-time classes during the internship period.
how_to_apply: Sign up for the Outreachy mailing list to be notified when the May 2027 round opens
Submit the initial application with essays (usually January–February)
If approved, contribute to one or more projects during the contribution period
Submit a final application for your chosen project
Interns are announced before the May start
outreachy-may-2027.costs: Free to apply. Interns receive a USD 7,000 stipend. Fully remote, no relocation.

ozclo-2027.about:
OzCLO is a volunteer-run contest in which teams of four develop their own strategies to decode problems about real languages and computational linguistics. Round 1 is held online on 17 March 2027; the best teams go to Round 2 on 29 March, which leads to the Asia Pacific Linguistics Olympiad (APLO) and selection for the International Linguistics Olympiad 2027 in Bangkok.

Teachers register teams through an OzCLO teacher account during the short February window.
highlights: Teams of four
Leads to APLO and IOL 2027
Run by volunteers, school-based
ozclo-2027.eligibility: Secondary-school students in years 7–12 at Australian schools, in teams of four registered by a teacher.
how_to_apply: Teacher creates an OzCLO account
Register teams between 19 and 24 Feb 2027
Practise with past problems
Compete in Round 1 on 17 Mar 2027
ozclo-2027.costs: Check the OzCLO site for any registration fee.

pakistan-hardware-hack-2027.about:
Pakistan Hardware Hack 2027 (TeenHacks) is Pakistan's first teen-only hardware hackathon, with paths for new and experienced hardware builders. It takes place in person in Lahore from 2027-02-27 to 2027-02-28, organised by TeenHacks (Hack Club community event).

Participants team up, attend workshops, build a working project and present it to judges. Food and workspace are provided free; travel is usually self-funded unless the organisers announce support.
highlights: Free to attend
Teen-only, hardware focus
Paths for beginners and experienced builders
pakistan-hardware-hack-2027.eligibility: School students aged 13–19 (currently enrolled in school).
how_to_apply: Open https://teenhacks.org/ and register or apply
Form a team or join one at the event
Arrange travel to the venue
Build and present your project
pakistan-hardware-hack-2027.costs: Free to attend; travel and accommodation self-funded unless stated.

partnership-international-school-exchang.about:
Partnership International is a non-profit German exchange organisation (member of AJA, the association of non-profit youth exchange organisations) that sends school students abroad for 3-12 months. It offers the PI-Stipendium (5-12 months, all countries), the PI Youth Ambassador scholarship (3-12 months, all countries) and support for the Bundestag's PPP scholarship to the USA.

You may apply for one partial scholarship (plus PPP). Families can also use loyalty and host-family discounts, instalments and Auslands-BAföG; the scholarship fund is filled by donations. Apply with the online scholarship form after registering for a programme.
highlights: Partial scholarships for 3-12 months
Member of the AJA non-profit network
PPP support for the USA
partnership-international-school-exchang.eligibility: School students living in Germany registering for a Partnership International programme.
how_to_apply: Choose a programme with Partnership International
Fill in the online scholarship form (PI-Stipendium or Jugendbotschafter)
Interview
Optionally apply to the PPP (bundestag.de/ppp)
partnership-international-school-exchang.costs: Programme fee; one partial scholarship per applicant; discounts and Auslands-BAföG possible.

paypal-ai-hackathon-2026.about:
Entrants build or significantly update an application that integrates PayPal's developer APIs (in the free sandbox) with any AI tool, model or platform, then submit a demo video and project description.

Judging runs 1–15 December 2026 and winners are announced around 21 December 2026. Over 20,000 people have registered, making it one of the largest open fintech hackathons of the season.
highlights: $67,500 in prizes
Fintech + AI theme
Free sandbox, fully online
paypal-ai-hackathon-2026.eligibility: Individuals who are at least the age of majority where they live (usually 18+), teams of eligible individuals, and organisations. Standard Devpost exclusions apply (residents of US-embargoed countries/regions and certain other jurisdictions; sponsor employees). Check the official rules before entering.
how_to_apply: Register on paypalaihackathon.devpost.com
Create a free PayPal developer account
Build your AI + PayPal app
Submit before 12 Nov 2026, 12:00 pm PT

peace-first-youth-grants.about:
Peace First is a global non-profit that has engaged young changemakers in 166 countries. Its grants support youth-led projects that tackle injustice and build peace in their communities, from first-time project starters to established initiatives, together with coaching, impact trainings and a peer community.

Peace First focuses on youth and young adults (typically ages 16-35), though age rules vary by grant tier and call. It also runs an Ambassador Program and the Africa Youth Change-Maker Award.

Grant calls open through the year and are announced on the Peace First website and Instagram; applications are online.
highlights: Grants plus coaching for youth-led projects
Open to young people worldwide
Supports first-time and established initiatives
peace-first-youth-grants.eligibility: Young people (typically 16-35; varies by call) leading a project for peace, justice or community change. Open globally unless a call says otherwise.
how_to_apply: Read the Grants page and FAQs.
Follow Peace First's website/Instagram for the next open call.
Describe your project and the change you want to make.
Submit the online application.
peace-first-youth-grants.costs: Free to apply; grants fund your project.

penn-summer-academies-2027.about:
Penn's School of Arts & Sciences runs intensive two-week Summer Academies on the Philadelphia campus, each built around one field and taught by Penn faculty and researchers: Astronomical Techniques Research, Experimental Design, Forensic Science, Mathematics, Environmental Policy, Social Change, East Asian History, an Academic English & University Readiness Academy, and more, plus online seminars (e.g. genomics and bioinformatics, writing for researchers).

Admission is rolling until programmes are full, and only complete applications are reviewed (decisions can take up to six weeks), so applying early matters. Penn lists tuition and scholarship opportunities on its site; international students are welcome.
highlights: Ivy League academies taught by Penn faculty
Research-flavoured STEM tracks (astronomy, forensics, experimental design)
Rolling admission: early applicants have the most choice
penn-summer-academies-2027.eligibility: High-school students (grades 9–12, depending on the academy) from any country; English proficiency required (an English readiness academy is also offered).
how_to_apply: Choose an academy or online seminar for summer 2027
Complete the online application (transcript, essay, recommendation as required)
Apply early: admission is rolling until full
Check scholarship opportunities and pay tuition once admitted
penn-summer-academies-2027.costs: Paid: tuition (and housing for residential students) per academy; see 'Tuition and Fees'. Some scholarships available.

physicsbowl-2027.about:
PhysicsBowl is a multiple-choice contest based on a typical high-school physics course. Division 1 is for first-year physics students and Division 2 for second-year/advanced students; schools are ranked within regions (including international regions) by their top scores.

Teachers register and proctor the exam online during the spring window. It is a good warm-up for the F=ma exam and physics olympiads.
highlights: 40 questions, 45 minutes, in school
Two divisions by physics experience
International regions included
physicsbowl-2027.eligibility: High-school students registered by their physics teacher; schools worldwide may enter.
how_to_apply: Ask your physics teacher to register when registration opens in December
Practise with past PhysicsBowl exams
Sit the exam in school during the spring window
physicsbowl-2027.costs: Per-student fee paid by the school (see AAPT).

polish-mathematical-olympiad-78.about:
The Olimpiada Matematyczna is one of Europe's oldest and strongest maths olympiads. The first stage has a test part and an open, proof-based part; qualifiers sit the regional second stage and the national final, and the best are trained for the IMO and EGMO teams.

A scientific camp for top students follows in late May/early June 2027. Problems and solutions are in Polish.
highlights: One of Europe's oldest maths olympiads
Three stages, Nov 2026 to Mar 2027
Path to IMO and EGMO
polish-mathematical-olympiad-78.eligibility: Secondary-school students in Poland (younger talented students may also take part).
how_to_apply: Check the schedule and rules on the official site
Register through your school for the first stage
Sit the open part on 6 Nov 2026
Qualify for the 2nd stage (29–30 Jan 2027)

power-learn-project-1-million-devs-afric.about:
Power Learn Project (PLP) runs the '1 Million Devs for Africa' programme, a fully funded 16-week online software development course for young Africans. The curriculum covers programming fundamentals, web development (including full-stack JavaScript/MERN), databases and soft skills, delivered in cohorts with instructors and mentors.

PLP reports tens of thousands of applications and enrolments across many African countries, with a community, internships and job-placement support for graduates; some alumni become PLP mentors or founders.

Applications are made online through the 'Apply Now' button for the next cohort; there is no tuition.
highlights: Fully funded (no tuition)
16-week cohort with instructors and mentors
Pan-African community and job support
power-learn-project-1-million-devs-afric.eligibility: Young people in African countries with internet access and commitment for 16 weeks; check the application form for country and age details.
how_to_apply: Go to the PLP website and click 'Apply Now'.
Fill in the application form.
Complete any onboarding test or orientation.
Join the next 16-week cohort.

promys-boston-2027.about:
PROMYS is one of the oldest and most respected summer mathematics programmes in the world. Held at Boston University's Department of Mathematics, it gives about 60 first-year students (plus returning students) six weeks of intensive work on number theory: daily problem sets, lectures, advanced seminars and mentoring from undergraduate counsellors and research mathematicians. The aim is to learn to think like a mathematician, not to race through a syllabus.

Applicants must solve a set of challenging problems as the core of the application, submitted together with a transcript, short answers and a recommendation from a maths teacher or mentor. Admission is selective but open to students worldwide aged 14–18 who have completed at least 9th grade. Students in China can apply for full Yongren Fellowships; European residents aged 16+ may choose PROMYS Europe in Oxford instead (not both in the same year).
highlights: Classic number-theory immersion with research mathematicians and counsellors
Admission is based mainly on solving a challenging problem set
Need-based financial aid; full Yongren Fellowships for students in China
promys-boston-2027.eligibility: Students aged 14–18 by the start of the programme who have completed at least 9th grade (or equivalent) and are not yet enrolled at university. International students are welcome; good English is needed. Applicants may apply to PROMYS or PROMYS Europe, not both, in the same summer.
how_to_apply: Watch the PROMYS application page from January 2027, when the 2027 problem set is published
Work on the problem set and write up your solutions as one PDF
Complete the online form with short answers and upload your school transcript
Ask a maths teacher or mentor to submit the recommendation form (due a few days after the deadline)
If you need aid, have a parent complete the financial aid form by mid-March
Decisions are emailed by the end of April
promys-boston-2027.costs: Programme fee covers tuition, room and board in Boston (amount published with the application; check the site). Need-based financial aid is available, and some fellowships cover all costs including travel.

pyleamun-2027.about:
PyleaMUN is a non-profit conference hosted and run entirely by a Greek public state school in Pylaia, Thessaloniki, with a strict zero-fee policy. The 2027 General Assembly topic is 'The Universal Right to Truth: Establishing International Norms Against State-Sponsored Disinformation', with committees such as UNSC, ECOSOC, UNESCO, WHO, HRC and UN Women.

The conference runs 11–14 February 2027 at Pylaia (Pylea), Thessaloniki, Greece. It is open to secondary school students (school delegations or independent delegates). Working language: English.

Use the forms on the official site: School Registration 2027, Independent Delegate Application 2027, Student Officer (Round 2), Media and Staff applications. Free: no registration or participation fee. Participants cover their own transport, accommodation and meals. As at any MUN, delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions — hands-on training in public speaking, research and diplomacy that universities value.
highlights: 11–14 February 2027 in Thessaloniki, Greece
Zero-fee conference run by a public school
No fees at all
pyleamun-2027.eligibility: Open to secondary school students (school delegations or independent delegates). Working language: English. No nationality restrictions are stated; international delegates (including from Georgia and Qatar) can apply, arranging their own visa and travel.
how_to_apply: Open the official website (link below) and read the conference information and committee list.
Use the forms on the official site: School Registration 2027, Independent Delegate Application 2027, Student Officer (Round 2), Media and Staff applications.
Pay the delegate fee by the stated deadline to confirm your place.
Prepare a position paper using the committee study guides before the conference.
pyleamun-2027.costs: Free: no registration or participation fee. Participants cover their own transport, accommodation and meals. Travel, accommodation and visas are paid by participants unless stated otherwise.

qwer-hacks-2027.about:
QWER Hacks 2027 is a hackathon celebrating LGBTQIA+ people in tech, welcoming allies. It is an official Major League Hacking (MLH) 2027-season member event, held in person at UCLA in Los Angeles from 2027-01-16 to 2027-01-17. Participants form small teams (typically up to four; check the event rules), attend workshops and talks, and present a working prototype to judges at the end.

Food, workspace, Wi-Fi, swag and mentoring are provided free of charge. Beginners are welcome: MLH events run introductory workshops and expect many first-time hackers. Applications are handled on the event's own website; spots are limited and usually confirmed a few weeks before the event.

Hackathons are one of the fastest ways to build a portfolio project, meet engineers from sponsoring companies and practise teamwork under time pressure.
highlights: Free entry, food and mentoring
Official MLH 2027 season event
Build a portfolio project in one weekend
qwer-hacks-2027.eligibility: Students enrolled at a college or university (many MLH events also admit high-school students aged 18+, and some all ages 13+ with consent). Participants must follow the MLH Code of Conduct. International students may attend but must arrange their own visa and travel.
how_to_apply: Open https://www.qwerhacks.com/ and sign up for application updates or apply if the form is open
Form a small team or join one at the event
Complete the application and accept the MLH Code of Conduct
Confirm your spot when accepted and arrange your own travel unless reimbursement is offered
Attend in person and submit your project for judging
qwer-hacks-2027.costs: Free to attend; meals, snacks and workspace provided. Travel and accommodation are usually at your own cost unless the event announces travel reimbursement.

rcmun-xvi-2027.about:
RCMUN is the one-day Model UN hosted at Michigan State University, now returning for its 16th session and reaching younger delegates too, with outreach scholarships.

The conference runs 20 February 2027 at Eppley Center, Broad College of Business, Michigan State University, East Lansing, United States. It is open to middle and high school students. Working language: English.

Registration details are posted on the official site later in 2026. The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. Outreach scholarships are available. As at any MUN, delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions — hands-on training in public speaking, research and diplomacy that universities value.
highlights: 20 February 2027 in East Lansing, United States
One-day conference with scholarships
The delegate fee is published on the official registration page
rcmun-xvi-2027.eligibility: Open to middle and high school students. Working language: English. No nationality restrictions are stated; international delegates (including from Georgia and Qatar) can apply, arranging their own visa and travel.
how_to_apply: Open the official website (link below) and read the conference information and committee list.
Registration details are posted on the official site later in 2026.
Pay the delegate fee by the stated deadline to confirm your place.
Prepare a position paper using the committee study guides before the conference.
rcmun-xvi-2027.costs: The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. Outreach scholarships are available. Travel, accommodation and visas are paid by participants unless stated otherwise.

recurse-center-retreat-2027.about:
The Recurse Center (RC) is a self-directed educational retreat for programmers, based in Brooklyn, New York, with remote participation also possible. Participants ("Recursers") choose their own projects and learn together for 6 or 12 weeks, from beginners who can already write small programs to experienced engineers.

There is no curriculum, no grades and no tuition: RC is free and funded by its recruiting business, which helps alumni find jobs if they want. Batches start every six weeks; Winter 2 starts 4 January 2027 and Spring 1 starts 15 February 2027, with later batches through November 2027.

Applications close about two weeks before each batch starts or when the batch fills. Admission is by written application plus conversational and pair-programming interviews.
highlights: Free: no tuition, no grades, self-directed
In person in Brooklyn or remote
New batches every six weeks through 2027
recurse-center-retreat-2027.eligibility: Adults who can already program and want to get dramatically better. Open to people from any country; in-person attendees must arrange their own visa, travel and housing.
how_to_apply: Read the RC 'apply' page and choose a batch and length (6 or 12 weeks).
Submit the written application (about your programming and what you want to work on).
Do a conversational interview and a pair-programming interview.
Apply at least two weeks before your chosen batch starts.
recurse-center-retreat-2027.costs: Free (no tuition). Living, housing and travel costs in New York are not covered.

regeneron-sts-2027.about:
Regeneron STS, run by Society for Science since 1942, recognises original independent research by high-school seniors. Applicants submit a full research report plus essays, recommendations and transcripts through an online application.

The top 300 scholars are announced on 7 January 2027 (each receives $2,000, with $2,000 for their school); the top 40 finalists, announced 21 January 2027, travel to Washington, D.C. for Finals Week on 11–17 March 2027, with a public exhibition on 14 March and the awards ceremony on 16 March.

It is one of the strongest signals a US applicant can show to top universities, and finalists' travel and expenses are covered.
highlights: ~$3.1 million in awards; $250,000 first prize
Top 40 finalists flown to Washington, D.C. (11–17 March 2027)
Free to apply
regeneron-sts-2027.eligibility: High-school seniors in the US and its territories, and US citizens attending school abroad, in their final year of secondary school. Research must be the student's own work. Check the official rules for full eligibility.
how_to_apply: Finish your independent research project and write the research report
Create an account on the Society for Science application portal
Complete essays, upload transcript and recommendations
Submit before 5 November 2026, 8 pm ET
regeneron-sts-2027.costs: Free to enter. Finalists' travel and lodging for Finals Week are paid by the organiser.

revolutionuc-2027.about:
RevolutionUC 2027 is the University of Cincinnati's student hackathon. It is an official Major League Hacking (MLH) 2027-season member event, held in person at University of Cincinnati in Cincinnati from 2027-02-27 to 2027-02-28. Participants form small teams (typically up to four; check the event rules), attend workshops and talks, and present a working prototype to judges at the end.

Food, workspace, Wi-Fi, swag and mentoring are provided free of charge. Beginners are welcome: MLH events run introductory workshops and expect many first-time hackers. Applications are handled on the event's own website; spots are limited and usually confirmed a few weeks before the event.

Hackathons are one of the fastest ways to build a portfolio project, meet engineers from sponsoring companies and practise teamwork under time pressure.
highlights: Free entry, food and mentoring
Official MLH 2027 season event
Build a portfolio project in one weekend
revolutionuc-2027.eligibility: Students enrolled at a college or university (many MLH events also admit high-school students aged 18+, and some all ages 13+ with consent). Participants must follow the MLH Code of Conduct. International students may attend but must arrange their own visa and travel.
how_to_apply: Open https://www.revolutionuc.com/ and sign up for application updates or apply if the form is open
Form a small team or join one at the event
Complete the application and accept the MLH Code of Conduct
Confirm your spot when accepted and arrange your own travel unless reimbursement is offered
Attend in person and submit your project for judging
revolutionuc-2027.costs: Free to attend; meals, snacks and workspace provided. Travel and accommodation are usually at your own cost unless the event announces travel reimbursement.

rit-next-big-idea-high-school-2027.about:
Teams develop an innovative product or service idea, then submit a pitch video and business plan materials. Prizes and judging details are on the official Prizes page.

It gives deaf and hard-of-hearing students a showcase for entrepreneurial and technical talent and a first look at RIT/NTID.
highlights: For deaf and hard-of-hearing students
Pitch your product or service idea
Run by RIT/NTID
rit-next-big-idea-high-school-2027.eligibility: Teams of deaf and hard-of-hearing high-school students (see the official requirements page).
how_to_apply: Read the requirements and pitch guidelines
Form a team with an adult coach
Register between 11 Jan and 19 Mar 2027
Submit your pitch

rockefeller-ssrp-2027.about:
SSRP places high-school students in research labs at The Rockefeller University, a biomedical research institution with many Nobel laureates. Over seven weeks (9am–5pm, Monday to Friday) students carry out a mentored research project, take part in workshops on experimental design and science communication, and present their findings at the end.

Participation and application are free, and NYC transit is covered; need-based stipends may be awarded. Students outside the US are encouraged to apply, but RockEDU cannot help with travel, accommodation or visas, so it suits international students who have family or a safe place to stay in New York.
highlights: Real biomedical research in Rockefeller University labs
Free to apply and attend; NYC transit card provided
Need-based stipends possible
rockefeller-ssrp-2027.eligibility: High-school juniors and seniors (sophomores not eligible) who are at least 16 by 21 June 2027 and can attend the whole programme full-time. Students from outside New York and the US may apply but must arrange their own housing and visa.
how_to_apply: Create an account on the RockEDU student application portal
Complete the application essays
Ask recommenders to submit letters before the deadline
Submit by 4 January 2027, 5:00 pm ET
rockefeller-ssrp-2027.costs: Free: no fees; NYC transit card provided; need-based stipends may be awarded. Housing and long-distance travel are not provided.

ross-mathematics-program-2027.about:
The Ross Program, founded by Arnold Ross in 1957, is a six-week residential summer course in which students discover number theory for themselves through daily problem sets, lectures and discussion with counsellors. The motto is 'Think deeply of simple things'. In 2026 it ran from 14 June to 24 July at Otterbein University in Columbus, Ohio and at Rose-Hulman Institute of Technology in Indiana.

Most first-year students are 15–18. International students are admitted every year (several per year) and need reasonable English fluency; the programme is treated as a 'mathematical vacation' so a visitor visa usually suffices. The application includes short essays, a video, a teacher recommendation, a transcript and solutions to challenging maths problems.
highlights: Legendary programme in number theory with a 'learn by discovering' approach
Two campuses in the US Midwest
Need-based scholarships available
ross-mathematics-program-2027.eligibility: Motivated pre-college students, typically aged 15–18 (occasionally 14 or recent graduates). International applicants are welcome and need good English.
how_to_apply: Check rossprogram.org from winter 2026/27 for the 2027 application and problem set
Solve the admission problems and write up your solutions
Prepare short essays, a short video, your transcript and a teacher recommendation
Submit before the deadline (8 March in 2026)
If admitted, ask about need-based scholarships
ross-mathematics-program-2027.costs: Programme fee USD 7,500 (2026) covering six weeks of room, board, instruction and course costs. Need-based scholarships available; travel is rarely covered for international students.

rotary-youth-exchange-district-7390-2027.about:
Rotary Youth Exchange is Rotary International's long-term school exchange: a sponsoring Rotary club sends a student abroad for a school year, and a Rotary club in the host country arranges host families, school enrolment and a limited monthly spending allowance. Parents typically pay travel, health insurance and some other costs, while Rotary arranges travel and helps with visas; scholarships may be available in some cases.

In District 7390 the online application opened on 1 August 2026 and closes on 31 October 2026. Candidates then interview with their sponsoring club, attend district interviews on 14-15 November 2026 (with a mandatory day on 15 November to choose countries) and learn their host country on 31 January 2027. Students outside this district should contact their own local Rotary club, as every district runs its own timeline (usually autumn deadlines for the following year).
highlights: Host clubs provide room, meals and allowance
District interviews 14-15 Nov 2026
Other districts: ask your local Rotary club
rotary-youth-exchange-district-7390-2027.eligibility: High-school students sponsored by a Rotary club in District 7390 (age rules set by the district; ask your sponsoring club).
how_to_apply: Contact a sponsoring Rotary club in the district
Complete the online application by 31 Oct 2026
Club interview
District interviews 14-15 Nov 2026
Country reveal 31 Jan 2027
rotary-youth-exchange-district-7390-2027.costs: Host family room and board plus monthly allowance from the host club; family pays travel, insurance and other costs; some scholarships.

sailmun-2027.about:
SAILMUN is the first edition of a new school conference in Wassenaar, next to The Hague, themed 'From observation to implementation: Advancing change'. It includes an International Court of Justice.

The conference runs 13–14 March 2027 at Backershagenlaan 5, Wassenaar (near The Hague), Netherlands. It is open to secondary school students, individually or in school delegations. Working language: English.

Individual delegates and schools register through the forms on the 'Registration & Fees' page by 17 Nov 2026. Fees: individual delegate €50; school registration fee €45 plus €50 per person (delegate or MUN director). As at any MUN, delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions — hands-on training in public speaking, research and diplomacy that universities value.
highlights: 13–14 March 2027 in Wassenaar, Netherlands
First edition, next to The Hague
Fees: individual delegate €50; school registration fee €45 plus €50 per person (delegate or MUN director)
sailmun-2027.eligibility: Open to secondary school students, individually or in school delegations. Working language: English. No nationality restrictions are stated; international delegates (including from Georgia and Qatar) can apply, arranging their own visa and travel.
how_to_apply: Open the official website (link below) and read the conference information and committee list.
Individual delegates and schools register through the forms on the 'Registration & Fees' page by 17 Nov 2026.
Pay the delegate fee by the stated deadline to confirm your place.
Prepare a position paper using the committee study guides before the conference.
sailmun-2027.costs: Fees: individual delegate €50; school registration fee €45 plus €50 per person (delegate or MUN director). Travel, accommodation and visas are paid by participants unless stated otherwise.

salesforce-trailhead.about:
Trailhead is Salesforce's free online learning platform. Learners complete short modules and 'trails' with hands-on challenges in a free practice org, covering Salesforce administration, development, data, AI agents, marketing and business skills.

Completed modules earn badges and points that appear on a public profile, and the content prepares for Salesforce certifications (exam fees are paid separately), which are in demand in many job markets. A large global 'Trailblazer' community offers support and local groups.

Registration is free and open to anyone.
highlights: Free hands-on modules with practice environments
Badges that show skills to employers
Path to Salesforce certifications
salesforce-trailhead.eligibility: Anyone with an internet connection; content mostly in English with some other languages.
how_to_apply: Sign up for a free Trailhead account.
Pick a trail (for example Admin Beginner or AI).
Complete modules and hands-on challenges.
Optionally prepare for a Salesforce certification.
salesforce-trailhead.costs: Free; certification exams are paid separately.

salto-anchor-resilience-amarante-2027.about:
ANCHOR is a five-day Erasmus+ training course (22–28 January 2027, including travel days) in Amarante, northern Portugal, for 24 youth workers from Portugal, France, Spain, Greece, Bulgaria and Malta. It focuses on personal and professional resilience, burnout prevention and recognising mental-health challenges within professional boundaries (including Psychological First Aid).

Methods include nature-based sessions, an experiential mental-health board game, Theatre of the Oppressed, storytelling and World Café. Participants co-create the ANCHOR Resilience Toolkit, an open educational resource tested with students of Escola Secundária de Amarante. The course includes preparation (questionnaire, learning contract with a mentor) and follow-up dissemination at home.

It is organised by Associação Comunidades que Florescem with partners in France, Spain, Greece, Bulgaria and Malta; trainers are Ana Catarina Mendes and Abraham Azzopardi. Participants receive a Youthpass.
highlights: Hands-on resilience and burnout-prevention training with a co-created toolkit
Nature-based, theatre and game-based non-formal methods
Accommodation and meals covered, travel reimbursed (EUR 285–395), Youthpass
salto-anchor-resilience-amarante-2027.eligibility: Youth workers aged 22+ with at least two years of experience who currently work with young people, resident in Portugal, France, Spain, Greece, Bulgaria or Malta (the SALTO listing reserves 4 places for applicants from Spain via Asociación Sociocultural BreGal). Working English required; commitment to preparation, the full week and follow-up. Youth workers supporting young people with fewer opportunities are encouraged.
how_to_apply: Open the SALTO training page and read the full description.
Create a free SALTO account and log in.
Complete the online application form before 8 November 2026 (24h UTC).
Wait for the selection result (around 22 November 2026) and arrange travel with your sending organisation.
salto-anchor-resilience-amarante-2027.costs: Funded by Erasmus+. Accommodation and meals fully covered (arrival dinner to departure breakfast). Travel reimbursed up to EUR 285 (green travel) to EUR 395 depending on the sending country, after documentation and dissemination are completed. The SALTO listing mentions a EUR 30 membership fee for new members of the Spanish partner.

salto-jahrestagung-fachkraefte-im-blick-.about:
JUGEND für Europa (the German National Agency for Erasmus+ Youth and the European Solidarity Corps) and IJAB (the German specialist centre for international youth work) hold their annual conference "Fachkräfte im Blick" on 17–18 February 2027 at the Gustav-Stresemann-Institut in Bonn. It brings together around 100 professionals and managers from child and youth services in Germany and German-speaking countries, plus researchers and youth-policy representatives.

The programme opens with keynotes from the heads of IJAB and JUGEND für Europa on European and international youth work in the current geopolitical situation, followed by three participatory formats: peer cafés, 'spotlights' where organisations present tools and methods, and thematic workshops with experts. Participants' needs collected at registration shape the programme.

The working language is German. The venue is accessible to people with disabilities.
highlights: Networking with the main German-speaking actors in European youth work
Participatory format: peer cafés, spotlights, thematic workshops
Accommodation and meals covered by the organisers
salto-jahrestagung-fachkraefte-im-blick-.eligibility: Professionals, trainers, project managers, youth-policy makers and researchers in youth work from Germany, Austria, the German-speaking Community of Belgium, Czechia, Liechtenstein and Luxembourg (as listed on SALTO). Good German is required.
how_to_apply: Read the event page in the SALTO European Training Calendar.
Log in to SALTO (free account) and submit the registration form, stating your needs and interests.
Apply by 11 November 2026.
Selection is communicated by 4 December 2026; participants from outside Germany coordinate travel reimbursement with their own National Agency.
salto-jahrestagung-fachkraefte-im-blick-.costs: Accommodation and meals covered by the organisers. Participants from Germany receive travel reimbursement minus a EUR 25 participation fee (waived for the Bonn region). For participants from Austria, Belgium, Liechtenstein, Luxembourg and Switzerland, travel reimbursement and any fee are set by their own National Agencies.

salto-ladder-to-inclusion-online-course.about:
Ladder to Inclusion is a free self-paced online course run by the Hungarian youth NGO Élményakadémia (Academy of Experience) with Associazione JOINT, Asociación Las Niñas del Tul and MARTA Centres. It helps youth workers and organisations make international youth mobility (youth exchanges, volunteering, ESC and other non-formal learning projects) safer, more inclusive and empowering for highly vulnerable young people.

The course covers safeguarding, risk management, trauma-informed and solution-focused approaches, preparing and supporting participants before, during and after a mobility, professional boundaries, crisis response and self-care, using practical examples and reflection exercises. It is aimed at youth workers, trainers, youth leaders, project managers, volunteering mentors, coaches and teachers; up to 500 participants, in English.

It is listed on the SALTO-YOUTH European Training Calendar for Erasmus+ Programme countries, Partner Countries Neighbouring the EU (including Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Moldova and Ukraine) and other countries. There is no fee, and you can start any time after registering.
highlights: Free, self-paced English e-course; start any time
Safeguarding, risk management and trauma-informed practice for youth mobilities
Open to residents of Georgia and other Eastern Partnership countries
salto-ladder-to-inclusion-online-course.eligibility: Youth workers, trainers, youth leaders, project managers, volunteering mentors, coaches and teachers resident in Erasmus+ Programme countries, Partner Countries Neighbouring the EU (Georgia included) or other countries of the world. Working language: English.
how_to_apply: Create a free account on the SALTO-YOUTH European Training Calendar.
Open the course page and click "Apply now!" to fill in the short application form.
Once registered, follow the link to the online course platform and start at your own pace.
salto-ladder-to-inclusion-online-course.costs: No participation fee. Online, so there are no travel or accommodation costs.

salto-sharing-paths-young-families-finla.about:
Sharing Paths, Strengthening Families is a study visit hosted by Metsäkartano, one of Finland's national youth centres, specialised in youth work, outdoor and adventure education and international youth work. The SALTO listing gives 6 February 2027 as the date. It gathers about 25 professionals from Erasmus+ programme countries who support young parents (under 30) and young families.

The programme combines study visits, workshops and professional exchange, including a joint exchange day with Finnish professionals. Focus areas are youth work, non-formal learning, inclusion, equal opportunities and cross-sectoral cooperation between youth work, family work and social services.

The organiser states clearly that the activity is for working professionals, not students. Application is through the organiser's form linked on the SALTO page.
highlights: Hosted by a Finnish national youth centre with strong international experience
Study visits plus a joint exchange day with Finnish practitioners
Travel grant based on the Erasmus+ distance bands
salto-sharing-paths-young-families-finla.eligibility: Youth workers, family-support professionals, social workers and NGO staff from Erasmus+ programme countries who work directly with young parents (especially under 30). Practical experience required; working language English. Not open to students.
how_to_apply: Read the activity description on the SALTO page.
Fill in the organiser's application form (Google Form linked on the page) by 1 December 2026 (Finnish applicants by 1 January 2027).
Wait for the selection result (by early January 2027).
Book travel within the Erasmus+ travel band for your distance.
salto-sharing-paths-young-families-finla.costs: Erasmus+-funded. Travel grant by distance band (e.g. EUR 211/285 green for 100–499 km, EUR 309/417 for 500–1,999 km, EUR 395/535 for 2,000–2,999 km). Accommodation and meals are expected to be provided by the host; contact the organiser for details.

salto-youth-plus-volunteering-fewer-oppo.about:
Youth+ is a free self-paced online course by Academy of Experience (Élményakadémia) with Outward Bound Romania, Via KreAction and Marta Centre. It teaches youth workers, teachers and facilitators how to support groups of young people with fewer opportunities to create and carry out their own volunteering projects, and is also useful for anyone mentoring ESC volunteers or groups.

The course is built on the field-tested "From Us to You" programme, used since 2011 with Hungarian young people in foster care and segregated minority communities, and gives an overview of experiential education, solution-focused and trauma-informed approaches. Up to 500 participants; working language English; a Youthpass certificate is available. The course is still in beta and asks for feedback through built-in forms.

It is listed on the SALTO-YOUTH European Training Calendar for Erasmus+ Programme countries, Partner Countries Neighbouring the EU (Georgia included) and other countries. No fee; start any time after registering.
highlights: Free, self-paced English e-course with Youthpass
Practical method for youth-led volunteering with young people with fewer opportunities
Open to residents of Georgia and the Eastern Partnership
salto-youth-plus-volunteering-fewer-oppo.eligibility: Youth workers, teachers, facilitators, youth leaders, project managers, volunteering mentors and coaches resident in Erasmus+ Programme countries, Partner Countries Neighbouring the EU (Georgia included) or other countries of the world. Working language: English.
how_to_apply: Create a free account on the SALTO-YOUTH European Training Calendar.
Open the course page and click "Apply now!" to submit the short application form.
Follow the link you receive to the course platform and complete the modules at your own pace.
salto-youth-plus-volunteering-fewer-oppo.costs: No participation fee. Online, so there are no travel or accommodation costs.

sasmun-xiv-2026.about:
SASMUN is the long-running Model United Nations conference of Schutz American School in Alexandria. SASMUN XIV takes place on 19–21 November 2026 on the school campus, with committees including the Security Council, ECOSOC and DISEC as well as crisis-style bodies for experienced delegates.

Schools can register a delegation (group rates, faculty advisor included) and students can register as independent delegates; chair applications are free of charge and include preparatory meetings.

A well-established Alexandria conference that welcomes both first-timers and experienced delegates from Egypt and the region.
highlights: 14th edition at Schutz American School
School-delegation group rates or individual registration
Free chair applications
sasmun-xiv-2026.eligibility: Secondary-school students (school delegations or independent delegates). English is the working language.
how_to_apply: Read Conference Information and Committees on schutzmun.com
Open Register and choose School Delegation or Individual Delegate form
Pay the delegate fee as instructed
Attend 19–21 November 2026 in Alexandria
sasmun-xiv-2026.costs: Delegate fees shown in the registration forms; group rates for school delegations; travel and accommodation extra.

scholastic-art-writing-awards-2027.about:
Since 1923 the Scholastic Awards have recognised teens' work in categories from painting, photography and film to poetry, short stories and critical essays. Entries are judged first by regional affiliates (results on 27 January 2027); Gold Key works advance to national judging (results on 31 March 2027), with scholarships and a national celebration.

Past winners include many well-known artists and writers. Students may enter individually or through their teachers.
highlights: Art and writing categories
Regional then national judging
Scholarships for top work
scholastic-art-writing-awards-2027.eligibility: Students in grades 7–12, aged 13+, who attend school and live in the US, US territories/military bases or Canada (excluding Quebec); US schools abroad are not eligible.
how_to_apply: Use the Region Locator to find your regional deadline
Create an account on the Scholastic Awards portal
Upload your work in the right category and pay the fee (waivers available)
Submit before your region's deadline
scholastic-art-writing-awards-2027.costs: Per-entry fee (fee waivers available for students in need).

science-olympiad-national-tournament-202.about:
Science Olympiad teams compete in a mix of written tests, lab practicals and build events (such as bridges, flying machines and robots). Division B is for middle school and Division C for high school. Around 7,000 teams take part in 450 tournaments; state winners qualify for nationals.

Teams join through their state chapter; invitational tournaments run through the autumn and winter.
highlights: Test, lab and build events
Middle (B) and high school (C)
National Tournament at Ohio State, May 2027
science-olympiad-national-tournament-202.eligibility: US middle- and high-school teams registered with their state Science Olympiad chapter.
how_to_apply: Start or join your school's team
Register with your state chapter
Prepare using the 2027 rules
Compete at regional/state tournaments to qualify
science-olympiad-national-tournament-202.costs: State membership and tournament fees; travel self-funded.

sciences-po-summer-school-university-pro.about:
The University Programmes of the Sciences Po Summer School bring students from all over the world to the Saint-Germain-des-Prés campus in Paris. Participants choose a Social Sciences track (core courses taught in English on politics, economics and international affairs, plus optional electives) or a French Language track, in a June session (7 June – 1 July 2027) and/or a July session (6–29 July 2027). A two-week Intensive Policy Lab runs 21 June – 2 July or 5–16 July 2027.

The programme is open to current university students, graduates and professionals, and to students in their final year of secondary school who will start university in autumn 2027 (younger students should use the separate Pre-College Programmes). There is no age limit; under-18s need parental consent. Sciences Po does not offer scholarships for the summer school.
highlights: Paris campus of France's leading social-science university
Choose social sciences (in English) or French language, one or two sessions
Certification/credit options and a short Intensive Policy Lab
sciences-po-summer-school-university-pro.eligibility: University students and graduates of any nationality, and final-year secondary students who will receive their diploma by summer 2027 and enrol in higher education in autumn 2027. English proof required (TOEFL/IELTS-type certificate or Sciences Po's free English assessment).
how_to_apply: Choose a track (Social Sciences or French Language) and session(s)
Prepare transcripts and English-language evidence (or take the free Summer School English assessment)
Apply online once the 2027 application opens and pay the EUR 50 application fee
If admitted, pay a EUR 600 deposit within one week and the balance within two weeks
Register for courses early (first-come, first-served)
sciences-po-summer-school-university-pro.costs: 2026 tuition: EUR 2,900 for one session, EUR 5,200 for two (EUR 5,000 early bird); Intensive Policy Lab EUR 2,200; optional elective EUR 500; application fee EUR 50. Housing, food and travel not included. No scholarships from Sciences Po.

scmun-xiv-2027.about:
SCMUN is a student-run high-school Model UN held on the USC campus in Los Angeles, now in its 14th session.

The conference runs 27–28 February 2027 at the University of Southern California campus, Los Angeles, United States. It is open to high school students and school delegations. Working language: English.

Use 'Register Now' on the official site. The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. As at any MUN, delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions — hands-on training in public speaking, research and diplomacy that universities value.

Hosted on the USC campus
The delegate fee is published on the official registration page

Use 'Register Now' on the official site.
Pay the delegate fee by the stated deadline to confirm your place.
Prepare a position paper using the committee study guides before the conference.
scmun-xiv-2027.costs: The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. Travel, accommodation and visas are paid by participants unless stated otherwise.

scotmun-xx-2027.about:
ScotMUN is Scotland's flagship university MUN, run by the University of Edinburgh Model UN Society; the 2027 conference marks 20 years of the event.

The conference runs 5–7 March 2027 at the University of Edinburgh, United Kingdom. It is open to university students. Working language: English.

Delegate and delegation applications are announced on the official site. The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. As at any MUN, delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions — hands-on training in public speaking, research and diplomacy that universities value.
highlights: 5–7 March 2027 in Edinburgh, United Kingdom
20th-anniversary edition run by EdMUN
The delegate fee is published on the official registration page

Delegate and delegation applications are announced on the official site.
Pay the delegate fee by the stated deadline to confirm your place.
Prepare a position paper using the committee study guides before the conference.
scotmun-xx-2027.costs: The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. Travel, accommodation and visas are paid by participants unless stated otherwise.

scvmun-lvi-2027.about:
SCVMUN is one of the oldest and largest high-school Model UN conferences on the US West Coast, now holding its 56th session.

The conference runs 29–30 January 2027 at Silicon Valley (Santa Clara Valley), California, San Jose, United States. It is open to high school students and school delegations. Working language: English.

Register on the official site: regular registration from 1 Oct 2026, late registration from 10 Dec 2026, registration closes 15 Jan 2027. The delegate fee is published on the official registration page. Fees rise at the late-registration stage. As at any MUN, delegates research their assigned country, write position papers, give speeches, negotiate in caucuses and draft resolutions — hands-on training in public speaking, research and diplomacy that universities value.

56th session of a West-Coast classic

Register on the official site: regular registration from 1 Oct 2026, late registration from 10 Dec 2026, registration closes 15 Jan 2027.
Pay the delegate fee by the stated deadline to confirm your place.
Prepare a position paper using the committee study guides before the conference.

seaperch-international-challenge-2027.about:
SeaPerch, run by the nonprofit RoboNation, introduces students to marine engineering: teams build a SeaPerch ROV, then test it in pool-based obstacle and mission courses and present an engineering notebook. Regional competitions across the US and in several other countries feed into the International Challenge.

Kits are low-cost and the programme provides curriculum for teachers, making it an accessible first robotics competition.
highlights: Build an underwater ROV from a kit
Regional events feed the international final
Low-cost entry robotics
seaperch-international-challenge-2027.eligibility: Middle- and high-school teams registered through a SeaPerch regional competition (mostly US; some international regionals).
how_to_apply: Get a SeaPerch kit and register on seaperch.org
Build and test your ROV
Compete at a regional SeaPerch event
Qualify for the International Challenge in June 2027
seaperch-international-challenge-2027.costs: Kit and registration costs (see seaperch.org); travel self-funded.

sf-hacks-2027.about:
SF Hacks 2027 is San Francisco State University's student hackathon. It is an official Major League Hacking (MLH) 2027-season member event, held in person at San Francisco State University in San Francisco from 2027-02-19 to 2027-02-21. Participants form small teams (typically up to four; check the event rules), attend workshops and talks, and present a working prototype to judges at the end.

Food, workspace, Wi-Fi, swag and mentoring are provided free of charge. Beginners are welcome: MLH events run introductory workshops and expect many first-time hackers. Applications are handled on the event's own website; spots are limited and usually confirmed a few weeks before the event.

Hackathons are one of the fastest ways to build a portfolio project, meet engineers from sponsoring companies and practise teamwork under time pressure.
highlights: Free entry, food and mentoring
Official MLH 2027 season event
Build a portfolio project in one weekend
sf-hacks-2027.eligibility: Students enrolled at a college or university (many MLH events also admit high-school students aged 18+, and some all ages 13+ with consent). Participants must follow the MLH Code of Conduct. International students may attend but must arrange their own visa and travel.
how_to_apply: Open https://sfhacks.io/ and sign up for application updates or apply if the form is open
Form a small team or join one at the event
Complete the application and accept the MLH Code of Conduct
Confirm your spot when accepted and arrange your own travel unless reimbursement is offered
Attend in person and submit your project for judging
sf-hacks-2027.costs: Free to attend; meals, snacks and workspace provided. Travel and accommodation are usually at your own cost unless the event announces travel reimbursement.
